task.title: Which statements answer a sub-question, and is it fully answered?
task.description: Read a question, one of its sub-questions and a short answer split into statements. Tick the statements that help answer the sub-question and say whether they answer it fully.

questions.text: Which statements help answer the **sub-question**? Tick every statement that gives part or all of its answer.
questions.none_label: None of the statements helps answer it

questions.text: Taken together, do the statements **fully answer** the sub-question?
What information is missing? Write one short sentence.

instructions.summary: For one **sub-question**, tick the statements that help answer it, then say whether the statements answer it **fully**.
instructions.background: A question was split into smaller sub-questions, and an automatic system answered the whole question with a few short statements. We want to know which statements answer each sub-question and whether any part of the sub-question is left unanswered.

criteria.label: Relevant
criteria.text: The statement gives part or all of the answer to this sub-question. Background facts that do not answer it are not relevant.

criteria.label: Fully answered
criteria.text: The ticked statements together answer every part of the sub-question.

criteria.label: Not fully answered
criteria.text: An important part of the answer is missing, or no statement answers the sub-question. Then write in one sentence what is missing.

steps: Read the original question and the sub-question.
Read every statement and tick each one that helps answer the sub-question. If none does, tick **None of the statements helps answer it**.
Decide whether the ticked statements answer the sub-question fully.
If you chose **Not fully answered**, write what information is missing.
notes: Judge only whether a statement answers the sub-question, not whether it is true.
A statement can help answer a sub-question even if it uses different words.
The same statements appear with every sub-question of the question; judge each sub-question on its own.
instructions.tip: Ask yourself: if this were the only text I had, would I know the answer to the sub-question?

planner_notes: One item is one entry of the subquestions map, shown with the original question and all statements of answer.system_a, the answer the prompt asks about. The relevance labels list the selected statement keys per sub-question, so the multi_select hint checks whether that list contains the statement key; the coverage labels are keyed by the same sub-question keys and map Covered/Not covered onto the two options. The missing-information text is required only when a worker chooses Not fully answered, and the attention item swaps in the question and sub-question of another record so that no statement is relevant.
